$comment: Test vectors for cov-v2 (ops decisions D48 item 5 and D82 item 10). Same rules as coverage/vectors.json, which stays frozen for cov-v1: every input is a COMPLETE published artifact (scripts/check-vectors.mjs validates each `repos` fixture against repo-record.v1.json, each `company` against entitlement-record.v1.json and each `waivers` document against waiver.v1.json), and `expect` is asserted by DEEP EQUALITY against the whole outcome. The first 25 vectors are cov-v1's, CARRIED: `carriedFrom` names the cov-v1 vector, whose inputs they repeat byte for byte, and whose expected result they repeat with exactly two moves — `basis.algoVersion` says cov-v2, and a `verified` record is reported as `registered` (D82's dated note (d)); coverage/cov-v2.test.ts proves both. The V2- vectors are new: (a) a Pass inside its term covers a work with no published record (`repo: null`, `repoNodeId` names the repository asked about, and nothing is published at registry/repo/{repoNodeId}.json; the answer reports `repoState: no-record`), and every other organisation gets `repo_not_registered`, expected as `{error, algoVersion, repo}`; (b) a registered repository its admins never claimed answers like any registered one; (c) the one public state. Vectors are appended, never edited, once cov-v2 is published.
emptyWaiversComment: The honest empty state, reused by every vector whose repository has no waiver. It deliberately carries no `nodeId`, so one document can stand for whichever repository is under test; a real published artifact always names its repository.

vectors.description: An active Pass covers every work under the licence, registered or not (D48 item 5) — no scope check, which is why it wins the precedence order.
A Project term matches a repository node_id named in its scope.
A Portfolio term matches the repo record's owner organisation id — not the owner login, which is a display cache.
A Portfolio term does not leak across owners: a different organisation's repository answers no.
THE REACHABILITY VECTOR (D14): a waived organisation with no account and no verified domain still answers yes, because the grant minted an unverified co_ stub the waiver names.
A waiver still inside its 72-hour cooling window is covered exactly like any other. Cooling governs whether VESTING attaches permanently, never today's answer (5th collision).
Revocation is prospective: once revoked, coverage stops, while the certificate verify record still attests the historical window.
A waiver naming a domain matches a company whose domains are DOMAIN-VERIFIED.
ANTI-SPOOF: a domain on a company that is NOT domain-verified matches nothing. Otherwise anyone could claim another organisation's waiver by asserting their domain.
vectors.fsRef: FS-10 §4.3 step 2 (verified-domain equality — the word 'verified' is load-bearing)

vectors.description: The residual step-3 branch: no company record resolved at all, yet a live waiver names the domain the caller was given. Answers yes-via-waiver — there is no entitlement record for a lane answer to outrank.
An active donation-lane term answers after waivers, per the step order.
Absence of a record is `no`, never an error — legibility for scanners.

basis.note: no registry record for this organization

vectors.description: Grace is DERIVED from the dates and is never a published status: periodEnd < now <= graceEnd.
BOUNDARY: now == periodEnd is still inside the paid term. A term does not evaporate on its last instant.
BOUNDARY: now == graceEnd is still grace.
BOUNDARY: one millisecond past graceEnd the answer is no. No dunning, no enforcement posture — just an honest no.
CHARGEBACK: a suspended term is excluded from every step and answers no immediately, within one publish batch of the notice.
A voided term (refund, or upheld chargeback) is void ab initio and contributes nothing.
An organisation holding a SUSPENDED Pass and an ACTIVE Project answers yes-via-project: the suspension filter runs before lane precedence.

WAIVER-FIRST ORDERING, the other half: eligibility is computed before any company short-circuit, but it is ANSWERED after lane precedence — so a payer who also holds a waiver answers yes-via-pass, the truthful stronger basis.
A live threshold self-certification answers under-threshold and still carries the entitlement-JWS proof, because the registration block travels inside that same signed record.
An expired registration falls through and coverage reverts toward no.
Precedence: a paying organisation that also self-certified under-threshold answers yes-via-project. The threshold answer is a fall-through, not a preference.
A delisted or quit repository still computes: entitlements and vesting stand (D12). The state travels in the basis so a caller can say so out loud, and the BADGE goes neutral independently.
A Project term covers the repositories its scope names and no others — the scope is the paid coverage, never the usage declaration.

A repository with no published record is covered by an active Pass: a Pass covers any work under the licence, registered or not. The basis says no record is published under the node id (`no-record`, which checks neither registration nor the licence) and why the answer holds.
vectors.fsRef: D48 item 5; D82 item 10; FS-10 §4.3 step 5a

vectors.description: The term boundary is the registered repository's: now == periodEnd is still inside the Pass, so a work with no record is still covered.
Two live Pass terms: the basis names the one with the later periodEnd, by step 5a's own tie-break, so two deployments name the same term.
A Project naming other repositories never reaches a work with no record: without a Pass inside its term the question stays repo_not_registered, as under cov-v1.
No company record and no record for the repository: repo_not_registered, never `no` — the organisation's absence is an answer only about a registered repository.
A suspended Pass is excluded exactly as at step 4, so it reaches nothing: repo_not_registered.
Only a Pass inside its term is answered about a work with no record. A Pass in its grace window answers lapsed-in-grace about a registered repository (VEC-13's rule) and repo_not_registered here.
A threshold self-certification is not an Entitlement, and cov-v2 answers only a Pass inside its term about a work with no record (D82 item 10): repo_not_registered, as under cov-v1.
vectors.fsRef: D48 item 5; D82 item 10; FS-10 §4.3 steps 1 and 8

vectors.description: A waiver is granted by a registered repository's admins and published under its record's node id; for a work with no record the waiver list is not read, even when one is passed.
vectors.fsRef: D14; D82 item 4; FS-10 §4.3 steps 1 and 2

vectors.description: A record published for a registered repository its admins never claimed carries `registered` and no claim status, and a Pass answers about it exactly as about any registered repository — no `reason`, because the record shows it.
vectors.fsRef: D82 items 1, 3 and 10; dated note (d); FS-10 §4.3 step 5a

vectors.description: A Project term naming a registered repository nobody claimed covers it: the claim adds admin powers, never coverage.
vectors.fsRef: D82 items 1, 4 and 7(a); FS-10 §4.3 step 5b; D42

vectors.description: A Portfolio term matches a registered repository's owner organisation id whether or not the repository was claimed.
An organisation with no record asking about a registered repository nobody claimed is answered `no`, never 404 repo_not_registered: the repository is registered.

basis.note: no registry record for this organization

vectors.description: A record published before D82 still says `verified`. It is read as registered and the answer reports `registered`, the one public state; the answer is VEC-02's.
vectors.fsRef: D82 dated note (d); repo-record.v1 1.4.0; versioning policy 4

vectors.description: A suspended repository is registered in D82 item 1's sense and its record shows `suspended`, as before; coverage that was bought still computes and the answer reports `suspended`.
vectors.fsRef: D82 item 1 and dated note (d); FS-10 §4.3 step 1; D12

vectors.description: VEC-03's Portfolio, asked about a work with no record. A Portfolio is matched through the record's owner organisation id, and with no record there is no owner to match: repo_not_registered.

VEC-11's donation term, scoped to the whole network, asked about a work with no record. cov-v2 answers only a Pass inside its term about such a work (D82 item 10), so the donation term stays repo_not_registered, as under cov-v1.
A void Pass is excluded exactly as at step 4, so it reaches nothing, a work with no record included: repo_not_registered.
A Pass whose term starts after `now` is not inside its term (step 5a skips it for a registered repository too), so it reaches no work with no record yet: repo_not_registered.

A Project whose scope names this very node id, asked about it while no record is published under it. cov-v2 answers only a Pass inside its term about a work with no record (D82 item 10), so the Project is answered once the repository's record is published, and until then the question is repo_not_registered, as under cov-v1.
vectors.fsRef: D82 items 1 and 10; FS-10 §4.3 steps 1 and 5b; D42

vectors.description: A repository that quit still has its record and still computes: coverage that was bought stays bought (D12). The answer reports `quit`, as published, never `registered`.
vectors.fsRef: D82 item 1 and dated note (d); FS-10 §4.3 step 1; D12
